enhanced.fullText:
The Oil Pollution Act (OPA) of 1990, codified at 33 U.S.C. §§ 2701-2762, establishes comprehensive liability and prevention requirements for oil pollution incidents in U.S. waters. Higher education institutions operating facilities that store, handle, or transfer oil products must comply with specific provisions under this federal environmental statute.

Under 33 U.S.C. § 2702, universities are strictly liable for removal costs and damages resulting from oil discharges from their facilities. This liability extends to cleanup costs, natural resource damages, economic losses, and third-party claims. The implementing regulations at 40 CFR Part 112 establish the Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) rule, which applies to facilities with aggregate oil storage capacity exceeding 1,320 gallons above ground or 42,000 gallons underground.

Key compliance requirements include: container inspection protocols under 40 CFR § 112.8, requiring visual inspections of above-ground storage tanks and associated piping systems; integrity testing programs per 40 CFR § 112.9, mandating pressure testing and non-destructive examination of storage vessels; comprehensive recordkeeping systems documenting all inspections, tests, and maintenance activities for minimum five-year periods as specified in 40 CFR § 112.7(e).

Universities must provide annual training to employees handling oil products, covering spill prevention procedures, emergency response protocols, and environmental protection measures under 40 CFR § 112.7(f). Additionally, institutions must conduct annual discharge prevention briefings for all personnel working near oil storage areas, ensuring awareness of pollution prevention measures and reporting procedures.

Enforcement authority rests with the Environmental Protection Agency under 33 U.S.C. § 2716A, which authorizes civil penalties up to $40,000 per day for SPCC violations, with maximum penalties reaching $137,000 per violation under current adjustment rates in 40 CFR Part 19. Criminal penalties under 33 U.S.C. § 2716A(b) include fines up to $250,000 and imprisonment up to five years for knowing violations.

Recent amendments include the 2016 SPCC amendments at 40 CFR Part 112, which modified inspection frequencies for certain storage systems and updated recordkeeping requirements. Universities must maintain current SPCC plans reviewed by Professional Engineers and updated every five years or following significant facility modifications.
enhanced.summary: Federal law requiring higher education institutions with oil storage facilities to implement spill prevention measures, conduct container inspections, maintain comprehensive records, provide employee training, and ensure strict liability compliance for pollution incidents.
enhanced.requirements:
## Facility Assessment and Planning
- Develop SPCC plans for facilities storing >1,320 gallons oil capacity per 40 CFR § 112.3
- Obtain Professional Engineer certification for SPCC plans
- Update plans every five years or after significant modifications

## Container Management and Testing
- Conduct monthly visual inspections of storage tanks and piping systems
- Perform integrity testing per manufacturer specifications under 40 CFR § 112.9
- Implement secondary containment systems for storage areas

## Training and Personnel Requirements
- Provide annual oil handling training to designated employees per 40 CFR § 112.7(f)
- Conduct annual discharge prevention briefings for all facility personnel
- Designate qualified individuals for spill response coordination

## Documentation and Recordkeeping
- Maintain inspection records for minimum five years per 40 CFR § 112.7(e)
- Document all training activities and personnel certifications
- Preserve integrity testing results and maintenance records
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Immediate notification to National Response Center (1-800-424-8802) for oil discharges per 33 U.S.C. § 2703. Submit written reports within 60 days of incidents exceeding reportable quantities. File SPCC plan amendments within six months of facility modifications.
